snippet.text: Solution: Pi's storage is working state and stays local, SQLite in a clone and thrown away on a runner. Hosts share the record through core's `RecordStore` port: add a batch of immutable records, list a changeset's records, fresh or not at all, one compare-and-set cell per changeset for the publication lease, and dispose. The contract assumes no ordering, history, transaction, secrecy or writer identity, so git, a directory, an object store or a database can meet it, and every adapter runs one conformance suite. The git adapter keeps `melian/state`, commits built with git's plumbing and never a checkout, `--force-with-lease` with backoff, and a wall-clock deadline; a record is a plain JSON file, and one commit holds a batch. Every store refuses a record past core's `recordLimit`, 4 MiB, and the relay takes a file up to that limit and a batch up to twice it. A guardrails record that would pass the limit keeps every finding's ID, severity and place. It leaves out the detail of its last findings in ID order, as [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605) asked. A notice's headline names the kind of each switch-off, such as changed npm scripts, so a trimmed notice still says it. Every other check's record gets the same budget, so Biome, tsc, Enola or mutation findings past it are trimmed alike. A record that cannot fit even so fails its check, and the review reads not reviewed, by the maintainer's ruling that [the decision](decisions/2026-11-20-guardrails-record-fits-the-store.md) records. The budget measures a check's own findings, not the record the review exports, so an exported record can still pass the limit, as the decision's known limits say, until [issue #626](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/626) lands. It builds commits in a bare repository of its own beside the clone, `records.git`, and fetches the branch's whole history into it. A file Melian did not write refuses work on the changeset whose folder holds it, or all work when it sits anywhere else, by [the am [cut at 2 KiB]

message.text: The added sentence says the tip keeps the records of pull requests "merged or closed in the last 30 days". That implies a pull request closed without merging is retired after 30 days. The code never retires one: `retire` removes only folders named in `merged`, and the retention decision keeps closed pull requests' records until issue #641.

That implies a pull request closed without merging is retired after 30 days. The code never retires one: `retire` removes only folders named in `merged`, and the retention decision keeps closed pull requests' records until issue #641.
explanation.whatToDo: Say that the tip keeps open pull requests' records, those merged in the last 30 days, and every pull request closed without merging until issue #641 lands.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md says: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." This change edited this exact sentence, and it now states behaviour the code does not have.

properties.failureScenario: A pull request is closed without merging and its folder is 40 days old. A reader of design.md expects it to be retired. In fact `retire` files it under `kept`, because `merged` does not name it, so the folder stays on the tip.
